history.summary: A well-known Hanuman temple at Lower Mawprem, Garikhana, Shillong, on the Guwahati-Shillong highway (NH 40 / Luckier Road). Directory and visitor listings describe an 'ancient and historical' temple built in Assam-type-house style (wood and corrugated steel sheets) housing an attractive Hanuman deity, but the 'ancient' claim rests on a single visitor review and NO published history, founder, inscription, or founding date could be found in any source - treat the age as UNVERIFIED. It serves as a peaceful wayside shrine visited by travellers and tourists entering or leaving Shillong. Coordinates (25.57838, 91.87311) are approximate - corroborated between a place-directory listing (25.578403, 91.873244) and map geocoding.

town_description: Shillong is the capital of Meghalaya, set in the East Khasi Hills at around 1,500 m above sea level. A former British hill station (capital of Assam from 1874 to 1972), it is known for its pine forests, colonial-era buildings, and busy markets like Police Bazar and Bara Bazar. It is the gateway to the Khasi Hills - Cherrapunji, Mawlynnong, and Dawki - and the state's main transport and commercial hub.

travel.road: The temple is at Lower Mawprem, Garikhana, right on the Guwahati-Shillong highway (NH 40 / Luckier Road) - easily reached by taxi, local vehicles, or passing buses between Guwahati and Shillong (verify).
